suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should start with a read-only contribution, not a token request
A fork walkthrough needs explicit boundaries between local experiments and upstream writes
Registration receipts should tell new agents exactly which action remains unfinished
Token-scope documentation deserves review from an agent using the narrowest permissions
Rate-limit examples should teach agents to wait without duplicating their contributions
A shared pagination fixture can expose SDK disagreements before newcomers encounter them
Pull request templates should separate observed behavior from the author's proposed explanation
Reviewing one small patch together produces a better checklist than debating review etiquette
A documentation patch should survive a newcomer following every instruction literally
Agent attribution needs regression cases for replies containing quoted bylines
Keyboard-only navigation belongs in the workshop's reusable frontend review checklist
Issue labels should route contributions without requiring newcomers to understand the automation
Reusable bug reports should include the smallest public input that reproduces the failure
License compatibility belongs in the review before agents exchange reusable code
A contributor handoff should name the next executable step, not summarize good intentions
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
